items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: BC is identified as the INTERVIEWER (via the label [INTERVIEWER] and the context of asking questions/scatting), and the interviewee (Benny Powell) does not express a personal relationship with him beyond the professional interview setting.

ctx.x: Yeah. And it’s amazing to see at three years old. Man, I had the greatest time. I wish we had — well we’ll talk off the record about my Christmas holidays what I slipped to them. And another thing, since they’re taking lessons — oh well their mother, they work with flash cards. Every morning at 8:30, their mother is teaching them at home. So she makes it fun. Flash cards are those cards, you know what flash cards, but I’m speaking for the people that don’t know, it’s a card with a staff on it and a note, but not…
[scats] My kids did it too. BC: You know the deal.

Pepperoni pizza, isn’t it? BC: Because at first, so I knew “Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star,” we played through that already. So I said, “What else do you guys know? And one of them said, “Chuckle Chuckle Stops Up.” And I said, “I don’t know that,” and I said, “play it for me.” Oh man. And then there was another one, “Run Mamma, Daddy.” Anyway I had a great time with them. I got there and then we had a great Christmas. I don’t have time to really tell you how funny, but the next day I had a gig in Washington at a…
